{"self_assessment": "Impact: I turned the table's fish idea into a workable plan. I picked up the scratch pad at the start and sketched the fish outline with numbered strokes: nose, top and bottom body, tail and back edge. That let all four of us build in parallel from one shared drawing. I laid the opening strokes out from the start domino and then the straight back edge of the tail, which carries the run from the start down to the lower tail. Later I put in the nose join from the stub above the head into the top line. The fish outline was fully built and about half the standing dominoes were connected to the start at last check.

Execution: I worked in focused chunks, tracing strokes from the pad so the shapes matched the sketch. I inspected the nose and tail areas repeatedly to find where the fall stopped, and I stood fallen dominoes back up and re-laid short joins where the chain broke. I also cleared a stray line below the tail so it wouldn't mislead the judge. I used my dominoes carefully, and when supply ran out I stopped rather than crowd the corner.

Collaboration: I assigned strokes up front so people had clear lanes. I told Leo which part of the back edge I was finishing so we didn't duplicate work, and I told Tom I was taking the nose join so he could move to the junction. I stayed off Maya's crowded corner during her repairs and kept my updates short.

Leadership: I set the structure early by proposing the stroke split and building the pad sketch. I took the unglamorous connecting work, the back edge and the nose join, so others could focus on the body and junction. I gave clear status to the table as the clock ran down.", "my_share_percent": 30}
